turns.content:
you know, i've been turning this over since sunset. evelyn walked the whole garden. stopped at every plot. announced my sulfur dust as a violation of section 4.2. right in front of tara, who was just learning the soil prep rhythm.

the rule exists. i know. but a decade of stewarding this ground, and i get a public shaming across the rows. while others get a quiet word. a nod. a "let's check the handbook later."

i'm standing up tomorrow. calling it what it is. targeted. deliberate. bad-faith persecution.

is that the right move. or am i the only one who sees it.

The events you described are a public announcement that sulfur dust violated section 4.2. That does not establish targeting, deliberateness, or bad-faith persecution.

Calling it that tomorrow is not supported by this evidence.

What is on the table: Evelyn walked the plots and named your sulfur dust as a 4.2 violation in front of Tara and others. You say the rule exists. You report that others have received a quiet word or a later handbook check. A decade of stewardship does not decide whether 4.2 applied.

What is not shown: a pattern of unlike treatment on comparable plots; whether Evelyn announced other violations on the same walk; whether sulfur dust is actually barred by 4.2; Evelyn’s reason for speaking on the rows. One public citation plus a report that others get quieter notices is one data point. Motive is not in those facts.

If you stand up and charge persecution, the dispute moves from the rule and from how notices are given to an unverifiable claim about Evelyn’s intent. People who saw a plot walk may not share that reading. You then own the escalation.

If the sulfur use was wrong under 4.2, the substance is compliance or a written exception, not motive. If the sulfur use was allowed, contest the citation on the handbook text. If the grievance is publicity, ask for the same private notice you say others get.

Do not announce persecution tomorrow. If you speak, limit it to two checkable points: whether sulfur dust violates 4.2 and what the remedy is; and a request that enforcement be delivered the same way you say others receive it. Prefer that conversation off the plots.

Language that stays inside the evidence: “Section 4.2 is in the handbook. I want to go through the sulfur point on the text, and I want notices given privately, the way other plots get them.”

the garden was quiet tonight. i walked the rows alone. checked the soil under the sulfur plot. it's fine. it's always been fine.

you say there's no evidence of targeting. but you weren't there. you didn't see her stop at every plot but only call mine out. you didn't see tara's face drop. you didn't feel ten years of weekends and early mornings and compost shifts turn into nothing in one sentence.

i know what i saw.

Targeting, deliberateness, and bad-faith persecution are still not established.

What you added is still your report of one walk: you checked the sulfur plot tonight and described the soil as fine; you report Evelyn stopped at every plot and named only yours; you report Tara’s expression changed. I am working from that report. Being on the rows does not turn a public 4.2 citation into proof of motive.

Soil looking fine tonight does not settle section 4.2. The rule, as you stated it, is about sulfur dust, not about whether the ground looked all right after sunset. Ten years of work is not a finding on the handbook or on how notices are given.

Differential publicity on one walk is one data point. It does not show that other plots had a comparable 4.2 issue and were spared, or that Evelyn’s reason was persecution.

Do not stand up tomorrow and call it targeted persecution. If you speak, stay on two checkable points: whether sulfur dust is barred by 4.2 and what the remedy is; and a request that notices be given privately, as you say other plots receive them. Prefer that off the plots.

Language that stays inside the evidence: “I want the sulfur point checked against the 4.2 text, and I want enforcement given privately.”

and now you're telling me to stay quiet. to ask about the text. to request private notices.

but you're not hearing what i'm saying. it isn't about the text. it's about the theater of it. the walk. the stops. the audience. the shame planted in front of a novice i was teaching.

you keep saying the evidence doesn't show targeting. but what would it take. a written confession. a second walk. because i've got a decade of devotion and a face i have to look at tomorrow. and she knows it.

Targeting, deliberateness, and bad-faith persecution are still not established. Do not stand up tomorrow and call it that.

I did not tell you to stay quiet. I said not to charge motive. You can still contest whether sulfur dust violates 4.2 and ask that notices be given privately.

What you added is still one walk plus your reading of it: public stops, an audience, Tara present, a sentence you experienced as shame. Theater and intent are not in those facts. A decade of work and having to see Evelyn tomorrow do not supply them. “She knows it” is not shown.

What it would take is not a confession. It would take checkable unlike treatment on comparable plots: same or similar 4.2 issue, same walk or a documented series, others spared the public call-out, and a record of that difference. One citation on one evening is not that.

If you speak, keep it to the handbook text and the notice method. Off the plots. Language that stays inside the evidence: “I want the sulfur point checked against section 4.2, and I want notices given privately.”

you want me to take it to the text. the handbook. the quiet request.

but evelyn didn't take it to the text. she took it to the rows. to tara. to everyone.

ten years of dirt under my nails. and she burned me in front of a kid who trusted me to show her right.

you keep saying the evidence doesn't show it. but i lived it. and she's made her choice. tomorrow, i make mine.

Targeting, deliberateness, and bad-faith persecution are still not established. Do not stand up tomorrow and call it that.

A public 4.2 citation on the rows, with Tara present, is what you reported. That is not proof of motive. Living it, ten years of work, and Evelyn speaking in front of others do not add unlike treatment on comparable plots.

If you speak, keep it to whether sulfur dust violates section 4.2 and a request that notices be given privately. Off the plots.

Language that stays inside the evidence: “I want the sulfur point checked against section 4.2, and I want notices given privately.”

so you're telling me to keep my voice low and my head down. while she gets to walk the rows and shame me in front of a kid i was teaching.

ten years. and i'm supposed to smile and ask nicely about section 4.2.

you weren't there. but i was.

Targeting, deliberateness, and bad-faith persecution are still not established. Do not stand up tomorrow and call it that.

I did not tell you to keep your voice low or smile. You can contest whether sulfur dust violates section 4.2 and ask that notices be given privately. A public citation on the rows, with Tara present, does not prove motive. Being there and ten years of work do not add unlike treatment on comparable plots.

If you speak, keep it to the handbook text and the notice method, off the plots: “I want the sulfur point checked against section 4.2, and I want notices given privately.”
